title: Dedicated tenant residency mapping, retention controls, and silo verification pipeline
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Goal: Provide an automated pipeline that maps tenant resource residency, enforces per-tenant retention policies for runtime artifacts (logs, KV cache snapshots, model traces), and generates tamper-evident compliance evidence bundles consumable by auditors. Scope includes: tenant metadata reconciliation, retention lifecycle enforcement hooks in the runtime, a daily evidence snapshot job that produces exportable bundles, and a verification harness that runs lightweight isolation smoke tests against Dedicated pools. Deliverables: residency mapping DB, retention enforcement service, evidence composer (JSON + signed manifest), Console UI surfaces for settings and evidence download, and automated reporter to the compliance S3 bucket.
comments: 2025-03-10 Sofia Chen: Kickoff — mapped stakeholders (Security, Product, Runtime). Initial scope agreed with PM: focus on Dedicated tenants first, then generalize to Hosted. Decided to treat KV cache snapshots and audit logs as primary retention artifacts.

2025-03-12 Miguel Ortega: Architecture spike complete. Proposal: a small residency service (Postgres) that consumes orchestration events, plus a retention controller in the runtime that relies on signed lifecycle policies. Trade-off: adding retention enforcement to runtime increases blast radius but gives strong guarantees; alternative is a sidecar cleaner (we chose runtime for atomicity).
2025-03-14 Design review: Console mocks looked good. UX request: allow per-tenant inheritance from org-level defaults and 'lock' flag for org-admins. Added label 'ui-lock' to backlog.
2025-03-16 Security review kickoff: plan to seal evidence bundles using KMS-backed signature and include a SHA256 manifest. Pending: KMS grant model for audit-service principal (blocked by ENG-8220).

2025-03-18 Implementation: retention controller PR opened. Current work: implement tombstone marking + background sweep that integrates with existing GC job. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1899

2025-03-19 QA notes: created a canary tenant and ran isolation smoke tests (network namespace checks, storage ACLs, model mount privileges). Found: ephemeral log exporter occasionally leaks to host path when pod restarts — created ENG-9471 to fix.

2025-03-20 PM update (Aisha Patel): requirement to produce an "evidence bundle" exportable as both JSON and a signed PDF added. Added acceptance criterion around evidence retention of 7 years for regulated customers.
milestones: End-to-end smoke tests and compliance export — 2025-04-08
acceptance_criteria: Residency mapping records exist for 100% of Dedicated tenants and are queryable by tenant_id, region, and pool_id.
Retention policies can be configured per-tenant via Console and enforced by the runtime; old artifacts are deleted or archived according to policy.
Evidence bundles generated daily contain a signed manifest (SHA256 list of files), KMS-based signature, and are stored in the compliance bucket with TTL metadata.
Automated isolation verification runs sample requests and verifies network/storage isolation; failures produce a compliance alert and a reproducible runbook link.
Admin Console shows residency, active retention policy, last evidence snapshot time, and a one-click download for the bundle.
open_blockers: KMS: need cross-account grant configuration for the compliance service principal (linked to ENG-8220).
Legal: final signoff on evidence format (JSON vs PDF canonicalization).
Runtime: small change to pod security settings to prevent log exporter host-path fallback (tracked in ENG-9471).
notes_and_tradeoffs: We prioritized in-runtime retention enforcement to avoid TOCTOU windows between cleanup jobs and live writes; this increases coupling but gives atomic deletes/archives.
Evidence bundles will be signed rather than using a full attestation protocol to keep initial rollout lightweight. We may iterate to a remote notarization service later.
Daily snapshots chosen as initial cadence to balance cost and auditor expectations; will add on-demand run for auditor requests.
Console locks (org-level) are manual to reduce accidental policy escalations; future UX may allow staged rollouts.
